title: Knights of the Zodiac
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Orphan Seiya earns the Pegasus Cloth, a constellation armor, and joins fellow Bronze Saints sworn to protect Saori Kido, the reincarnation of the goddess Athena. They fight through the Gold Saints' twelve temples to unseat a usurping Pope, then battle the gods Poseidon and Hades to save the world.
life_message: True strength comes from friendship, self-sacrifice and fighting only to protect others and justice.

content.note: Continuous martial battles to the death through temples and the Underworld (Wikipedia); Thompson calls it combat-oriented; AniList and MangaUpdates tag tournaments and super powers.
Underworld journey, deaths of allies, Seiya mortally wounded at the end (Wikipedia); Athena sacrifices her life.
Little romance reported; Wikipedia notes a large fan pairing culture, which is outside the text.
Battle taunts; not otherwise reported (to verify).
Saga takes his own life after his good side returns (Wikipedia). Single-source detail, capped (to verify).
Heroic fighting and enduring injury for friends.
Toy-friendly armor designs and a large franchise; no in-story product placement reported.

dominant: Classical virtue (courage, loyalty, sacrifice); Greek-myth paganism as setting; critique of tyrannical power

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Ikki's vengeance and personal duels decide every conflict; warriors answer challenges in person.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Saints sworn to a sacred order and hierarchy of Bronze, Silver and Gold ranks.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Brotherhood of Bronze Saints and Seiya's search for his sister drive loyalty.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Rigid cloth ranks and a goddess at the top; heroes defy only a usurper.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Greek mythology and reincarnated gods structure the world.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Endurance, training and sacrifice to survive battles dominate.

folkways.japan: Reflects 1980s Weekly Shonen Jump norms of friendship, effort and victory, with senior-junior rank among warriors and a Japanese reimagining of Greek myth.

delivery.evidence: Thompson notes friendship and sacrifice themes through action; no review on preachiness found (to verify).

personified.ideology: Defensive justice and love for humanity
Rule by force for a supposedly greater order

delivery.note: Opponents are mostly rival gods and warriors, with the usurper Saga given a split good and evil nature rather than a flat portrayal.

winners_losers: Athena and the Bronze Saints defeat Saga, Poseidon and Hades at great personal cost; loyalty and protective sacrifice win sympathy, conquest loses.
